round1_to_round2.convergence_assessment: The convergence is partly anchoring and partly genuine. All five now value pro forma using exactly my round-1 net-claims template: debt $5.42B, cash $0.668B, pension $0.573B, 282.8M diluted shares, about $0.9-1.0B FCF. These are verified primary figures, so agreeing on them is correct, not herding. The anchoring shows in the judgment inputs. Four of five credit Ma'aden at exactly $1.25B (the same 8% haircut) without checking its market value. The spread across agents at mid-strikes fell from about 0.023 to 0.017, while URL overlap rose (mean Jaccard 0.121 to 0.192, distinct share 0.733 to 0.658), mostly from citing the same SEC exhibits and my Reuters/Kitco sources. The remaining disagreements (5.0x vs 5.25x, AliGroup $0.6-0.78B, Ma'aden $1.15-1.25B) are reasoned and independent. Agents 2, 3 and 4 also brought new, checkable evidence: the Goldman cut date, the MS/BofA notes, China ingot draws and FOMC odds. The mean barely moved (+0.3 at FV, under 1 pt on the ladder), so round 2 adds precision on facts rather than new direction.

revision_check.note: Added the $573M pension and pro forma cash $668M, lifted standalone EBITDA to $2.3B to match its deck, dropped the unsourced WoodMac/CRU bull figures, moved to 5.25x. Each change traces to a checked primary figure. Its $1.25B Ma'aden credit (an 8% haircut) is the same number as agents 2, 4 and 5; nobody checked the market value, which was about $1.43B on 22 Sep.

Rebuilt pro forma as asked and raised P/E from 9x to 10x. Its one real independent contribution is dating the Goldman $2,700/t cut to 6 Jul 2026 (Newsquawk). I verified that date, and it corrects my round-1 file. It also keeps 5.0x and gives its reasons. Fair value is unchanged at $46 because the corrections offset each other; I checked that arithmetic.

Added Ma'aden and moved to a pro forma basis. It also added new checked evidence: the MS 8 Jul downgrade (verified: PT $53, aluminium ~20% below consensus, EBITDA 33-49% below) and BofA Underperform $51 (verified, 9 Jul). It confirmed the Ma'aden lock-up (verified: one-third transferable at each of the 3rd/4th/5th anniversaries of 1 Jul 2025; hedging and borrowing allowed). Two inputs overreach. AliGroup at $0.6B is below the memorandum's ~$0.8B through-cycle, an average that already includes weak-alumina years. The $1.15B Ma'aden credit leans on the Q2 $123M mark-to-market loss, but Ma'aden at about SAR 62.6 in late Sep values the stake at about $1.43B, above the $1.36B book value.

Cut EBITDA from $3.5B to $3.1B, added Ma'aden and raised tax to 30%. It also fixed its lane: China ingot draws (verified via SMM: -63/-55/-55kt in the three weeks to 30 Sep, steepest for that period in recent years, but pre-holiday and seasonal), the LME tape, and Polymarket FOMC odds (it gave 37%; the market showed 34% hike / 65% hold on 1 Oct). Its Tower Extrusion check of the Midwest premium (about $1.10) could not be verified because the page shows no 2026 data.

Rebuilt pro forma and de-clustered its base rate to n=6 episodes (a real lane contribution). It weighted post-spike analogs (2018, 2022: 0.74-0.82x), which is a judgment call with n=2. Its multiple (5.0x) and FCF ($0.9B) disagreements are reasoned.

fair_value.reason: Pro forma. EV/EBITDA: $3.05B normalized combined EBITDA (standalone ~$2.3B + AliGroup ~$0.73B + small synergies) x 5.1x = $15.6B, less net claims of ~$3.0B (net debt $4.75B + pension $0.57B - Ma'aden $1.3B - FCF $1.0B) = $12.5B / 282.8M = ~$44.3. P/E: EBITDA $3.05B - D&A $0.93B - interest $0.39B = $1.73B pretax x 0.70 = $1.21B / 282.8M = $4.28 x 9.5x = $40.7 + Ma'aden $4.6/share = ~$45.3. Blend about $44.5. This is $0.5 below my round-1 $45: Goldman's cut is no longer fresh and Ma'aden is worth a bit more, but I trim FCF and the multiple from 5.25x to 5.1x. It is $0.4 above the agents' $44.1 mean.
